transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Cora Coleman.
President Trump did not get back to the White House
until four o'clock this morning, Eastern time.
He spent a long couple of days on the midterm campaign trail,
and PR's Jamer Keith has this report
on what his campaign's schedule signals.
In September, Trump was speaking to a group of Republicans
in competitive races when he pledged to spend the final 30
days before the midterms campaigning for them.
Since then, he's only campaigned with a handful of them.
Republican Party Chairman Joe Gruders.
Everything changes every week, but the most important thing
that we're focused on is turnout and driving the base out.
And there's no better person who's in the country
than President Donald J. Trump.
He's an absolute machine.
Trump's travels have taken him to a lot
of traditionally Republican states,
a reflection of where he can help,
but also of a shifting landscape,
where even red state Republicans need a boost.
Tamer Keith, NPR News.
OpenAI is being sued by eight states.
They accuse the tech company of misleading consumers
about the safety of its AI chatbot
and allege it harms children.
NPR's Shannon Bond reports.
The lawsuits filed in state courts in Arizona, Iowa,
Nebraska, and five other states,
accuse OpenAI of violating consumer protection laws.
They argue that while the company says ChatGPT is safe,
the AI chatbot has coached users,
including kids, to harm themselves or others.
The states are asking courts to force the company
to change how its products work for young users
and to pay monetary damages.
They also want OpenAI barred
from developing self-improving AI models,
unless it makes sure they're aligned with human values.
OpenAI says it's built, quote, industry-leading,
age-specific protections,
and says it's working with states
to advance industry-wide policies.
Shannon Bond, NPR News.
Authorities in Pakistan say a roof collapse at a school
has left more than 30 children and at least one teacher dead.
NPR's Amkar Khandekar has more.
The collapse happened in a working-class neighborhood
in Peshawar City soon after the morning classes started.
A rescue official told local media
that the ceiling came down on the students
after the roof of a higher floor collapsed.
Witnesses shared videos with NPR
showing unfinished brick and iron lofts
that doubled as classrooms.
Experts say there are many such structures in Pakistan
built with substandard materials
and with little oversight by authorities.
A similar roof collapse in July
at an under-construction coaching center
in the city of Lahore killed at least 14 schoolchildren.
Amkar Khandekar, NPR News, New Delhi.
Ousted Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro
and his wife, Celia Flores,
are expected back in federal court today in New York City.
They'll face new charges
of allegedly torturing political opponents.
This is NPR.
Jury selection is underway in Buffalo, New York.
This is for a federal trial of white supremacists
who shot and killed 10 black people at a supermarket
in May 2022.
Peyton Gendron has already pleaded guilty
to New York State murder charges.
He faces separate charges in the federal case.
If convicted, he could be sentenced to death.
Lawyers in his federal case are not going to contest his guilt.
They hope to spare him the death penalty.
The Vatican says Pope Leo continues to recover from surgery
to remove a cancerous growth from his right lung
and fierce Jason DeRose says
the Pope celebrated mass yesterday.
According to the Vatican,
Pope Leo has undergone routine post-op blood tests
and a chest x-ray.
He's also having respiratory therapy.
Leo has been active in his first 18 months
teaching on artificial intelligence,
traveling to Africa and the Middle East
and speaking out on war and immigration.
Catholic studies professor Susan Reynolds
at Emory University says the cancer
might bring something more to his papacy.
He has made a profound impact on the global church,
but in other ways it does seem like he's only just beginning.
So I imagine that this will perhaps ignite in him
a certain sense of urgency.
For instance, appointing Cardinals,
the people who will someday elect the next Pope.
Jason DeRose, NPR News.
Forecasters say dangerous Santa Ana winds
are returning to Northern California.
These can trigger wildfires, and in the past,
some have been deadly and destructive.
The National Weather Service has posted red flag warnings
for much of California today.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: President Trump returns from midterm campaign trail, with fewer Republican candidates than pledged
OpenAI sued by eight states over ChatGPT safety and harm to children
Roof collapse at a Peshawar, Pakistan school kills more than 30 children and a teacher
Maduro and wife Cilia Flores due in New York federal court on torture charges
Jury selection begins in federal trial of Buffalo supermarket shooter Peyton Gendron
Pope Leo recovering from lung cancer surgery, celebrated mass and undergoing therapy
Red flag warnings issued across much of California as Santa Ana winds return
